title: Burrito Bowl, Beef or Pork, with Beans and Rice

content.title: About
content.content: The Burrito Bowl is a Mexican‑style dish served in a bowl with rice, beans, seasoned beef or pork, fresh vegetables and sauce. It combines the rich flavor of meat, aromatic spices and the nutritional benefits of legumes and grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burrito bowls are often served without a tortilla, making them lighter and easier to eat on the go.
Traditional Mexican restaurants use black beans, but red beans or pinto beans are also common.
The rice is usually cooked with lime and cilantro for a fresh aroma.
Meat is often marinated in a blend of chili, cumin and garlic to boost flavor.
The dish is popular among athletes because of its high protein and complex carbohydrate content.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef and pork provide a complete set of amino acids that support muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice and beans release energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Beans supply fiber that aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and legumes are good sources of B6 and B12, essential for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The bowl contains iron, zinc and magnesium, which support immunity and metabolic processes.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If the sauce includes soy sauce or a prepared dressing, the salt level can be high; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Meat fat content
items.content: Pork can contain more saturated fat; choose lean cuts or limit the amount.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A Burrito Bowl is a filling meal, so its energy content should be considered in a weight‑management plan.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bowl is eaten with a spoon, mixing all ingredients together. Add guacamole, sour cream, fresh lime juice or hot sauce to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared bowl in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the microwave or on a skillet, adding a splash of water to keep the rice from drying out.
